subject: health
unitTitle: Staying Safe at Home, Outside, and Online
essentialQuestion: How do I spot a hazard early and choose the safest next step?

prompts.prompt: Explain home and kitchen safety in your own words and give or identify a valid example.

Use a diagram of a general figure or character rather than your own body, a picture sequence, a model, a described demonstration, or a checked source, to show what you learned about emergency help and calling 911.
Apply what you learned about wheels, helmets, and street safety to a new fictional situation. Show the steps or name the source you relied on.
A made-up character makes an unsafe or unreliable choice involving water safety. Explain what is wrong, correct it, and say why the correction is safer.
Connect home and kitchen safety with device and online safety basics. Explain how the two ideas support or depend on one another.

Present the strongest evidence from the unit task: Make a household and outdoor safety plan with hazard checks, safe steps, an escape route, and who to contact. A guardian reviews and confirms the plan.
Name one skill you can now use somewhere else, one way to check your own work, and one question you still have. This is about the skill, not about your private life; nothing private has to be shared.
